Crop a semihawkes spatial background to its study-area sf polygon

Source: R/background-plot-utils.r
crop_background_spatial.Rd

Restricts the fitted spatial-background grid to the region the model was fitted on, instead of the full rectangular estimation grid, by intersecting each grid cell (as a small square polygon) with region.

Usage

crop_background_spatial(background, region, crop = TRUE)

Arguments

background

The background component of a semihawkes_fit object.

region

An sf/sfc POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON study-area boundary, typically fit$events$region.

crop

Currently unused; kept for interface compatibility. Cells outside region are always dropped (they have no intersection).

Value

An sf object with columns x, y, basevalue, and one (possibly clipped) polygon geometry per grid cell that overlaps region, ready for ggplot2::geom_sf(aes(fill = basevalue)).

Details

sf::st_intersection() between polygons can occasionally return mixed geometry types (e.g. a POLYGON clipped down to a LINESTRING or POINT when it only grazes the boundary, or a GEOMETRYCOLLECTION). ggplot2::geom_sf()/fortify() cannot handle a geometry column with mixed/non-standard types, so we explicitly keep only (MULTI)POLYGON results and cast them to POLYGON/MULTIPOLYGON.

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date",
                     end_date = "2022-01-01")
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
ev <- add_adaptive_bandwidth(ev, k = 5, min_dist = 150, min_bandwidth = 300)
ev <- add_bg_integral(ev, n_mc = 500, seed = 1)
bg <- background_spatial(ev, cell_size = 1000)
cells <- crop_background_spatial(bg, ev$region)
head(cells)
#> Simple feature collection with 6 features and 3 fields
#> Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 5500 ymax: 500
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 17S
#>      x y basevalue                       geometry

#> 2 1000 0 0.1176292 MULTIPOLYGON (((500 500, 15...
#> 3 2000 0 0.1557842 MULTIPOLYGON (((1500 500, 2...
#> 4 3000 0 0.2630437 MULTIPOLYGON (((2500 500, 3...
#> 5 4000 0 0.3389455 MULTIPOLYGON (((3500 500, 4...
#> 6 5000 0 0.3366383 MULTIPOLYGON (((4500 500, 5...
